title: Crawl with a concurrency limit
problem: Write fetch_many: download a list of URLs concurrently, but never have more than `limit` requests in flight, so you don't overload the remote server or run out of connections. Results must come back in the order of the input URLs.
requirements: Return the fetched bodies in input order
At most `limit` fetches are in flight at any moment
Use the limit fully: with more URLs than `limit`, exactly `limit` fetches run at once at some point
Errors from fetch propagate (inside an ExceptionGroup is fine)
contract: async def fetch_many(urls: list[str], fetch: Callable[[str], Awaitable[str]], limit: int) -> list[str]
expectedBehavior: fetch_many([12 URLs], fetch, limit=3) returns 12 bodies in input order, and the fake site saw a peak of exactly 3 concurrent requests.
edgeCases: limit larger than the number of URLs: all run at once
limit == 1: strictly one at a time
A fetch raises ConnectionError: it reaches the caller
hints: Conceptual: start a task for every URL, but make each one acquire a permit before calling fetch and give it back afterwards. The number of permits is the limit, exactly like a buffered channel used as a semaphore in Go.

Specific: create one asyncio.Semaphore(limit) per call of fetch_many and write a small inner coroutine that does `async with` on it around `await fetch(url)`. Run one of those per URL with a TaskGroup or gather.
Implementation: check limit first; define `async def one(url): async with sem: return await fetch(url)`; create tasks with a TaskGroup in URL order and return [t.result() for t in tasks].
evaluation: The semaphore is created inside fetch_many (not a module-level global shared by all callers)
Permits are released via async with, so an error can't leak a permit
